text:
Timing: 0:35-1:55

MEMORY ANCHOR: Coupled aquifer, sparse data, separate analyses, conflicting stories.

SAY THIS:
The problem is that groundwater residence time, flow-path connectivity and chemical evolution are physically coupled, but they are commonly analysed as separate inverse problems. In data-limited aquifers, each problem is already non-unique. Several age distributions may fit the same tracer signal. Several directed networks may fit sparse hydraulic evidence. Several reaction pathways may reproduce the same chemistry. When these analyses are performed separately, uncertainty from one stage is often treated as fixed truth in the next. The result can be several individually plausible but mutually incompatible aquifer stories. Even worse, combining evidence can make uncertainty appear smaller while the interpretation becomes less accurate. This creates a clear methodological need: a framework that links the evidence streams, tests whether local relations are globally compatible, measures whether each added stream contributes real information, and reports when the problem remains non-identifiable.

TRANSITION:
That problem becomes clearer when we examine how the three unknowns constrain one another.

DELIVERY CUE: Use the four-part rhythm: coupled system, sparse evidence, separate workflows, conflicting stories. Emphasise 'mutually incompatible'.

AVOID SAYING: Do not say that conventional methods are wrong. Say that analysing them separately leaves cross-domain consistency untested.

Timing: 1:55-3:00

MEMORY ANCHOR: Age, topology and chemistry constrain each other.

SAY THIS:
These three unknowns cannot be interpreted independently. Age evidence constrains plausible travel direction and residence time. Topology determines which samples can reasonably be compared along a flow path. Chemistry constrains which reactions are plausible between connected locations. Conventional sequential workflows often estimate one domain first and then pass that estimate forward as if it were known. HydroSheaf instead treats the relations themselves as uncertain. It asks whether locally plausible age, hydraulic and chemical relations can be assembled into a globally compatible interpretation. If they cannot, the conflict should remain visible rather than being averaged away.

TRANSITION:
This leads to one overall aim and four questions that can be tested directly.

Timing: 3:00-4:00

MEMORY ANCHOR: Recover, integrate, compare, and define the field boundary.

SAY THIS:
The aim was to develop, benchmark and apply HydroSheaf for the joint diagnosis of residence-time distributions, directed flow-path connectivity and hydrogeochemical evolution. I organised that aim into four questions. First, can the component methods recover known or reference behaviour? Second, when does one evidence stream add information to another? Third, what does affine sheaf structure contribute beyond ordinary weighted graphs? Fourth, given the actual Ghana data, what conclusions are supportable and what remains unknowable? These questions move from component verification to integration, then to methodological novelty, and finally to field relevance.

TRANSITION:
Before presenting the results, I need to separate the inherited scientific foundations from the thesis contribution.

Timing: 4:00-5:00

MEMORY ANCHOR: The novelty is coupling plus falsification, not inventing the ingredients.

SAY THIS:
The individual ingredients are established. The thesis does not claim to invent tracer dating, directed graphs, sheaf theory, PHREEQC, MODFLOW or MODPATH. The contribution is the way these foundations are made operational together for groundwater inference. HydroSheaf provides an executable coupling, treats uncertainty and identifiability as outputs, uses adverse controls to detect false confidence, applies locked claim-decision rules, and diagnoses the evidential ceiling of field datasets. The novelty is therefore methodological and evaluative: it is a local-to-global integration and falsification workflow, not a claim that every individual method is new.

TRANSITION:
The clearest way to see the additional representation is to compare a weighted graph with an affine sheaf.

text:
Timing: 5:00-6:20

MEMORY ANCHOR: A weight scores a relation; an affine map transforms it and tests compatibility.

SAY THIS:
An ordinary weighted graph describes which nodes are connected and assigns a scalar strength to each edge. That is useful, but it assumes that the quantities being compared share the same coordinate relation. In the scalar-affine representation benchmark, the sheaf used a static scalar affine relation: the state at one node was related to the other through an edge-specific gain and offset. This allows different edges to express different relations. The framework can then test whether those locally plausible relations compose into a global section, and it can localise incompatibility around cycles. The tested contribution is therefore scalar affine representation and conflict localisation. The broader software can represent multivariate stalks, but multivariate vector-stalk performance was not validated in this thesis.

TRANSITION:
Because different experiments answer different questions, I matched every claim to an explicit evidence level.

Timing: 6:20-7:40

MEMORY ANCHOR: Different evidence levels support different claims.

SAY THIS:
The validation strategy is staged. Unit and conversion checks establish that declared inputs are represented correctly. Reference emulation asks whether HydroSheaf can closely reproduce an established public workflow. Controlled known-truth benchmarks test recovery when the answer is planted externally. Field transfer asks what real observations can support when truth is unavailable. The missing highest level is a matched field dataset containing age tracers, repeated hydraulic observations, chemistry and independently measured connectivity. I also used locked tests. Development cases were used to select the method and decision rules. The held-out cases were then opened once for confirmatory evaluation. This prevents favourable test results from being created through repeated tuning.

TRANSITION:
With that claim structure in place, I first checked whether the basic architecture worked under controlled conditions.

text:
Timing: 8:35-10:25

MEMORY ANCHOR: Close agreement, no robust graph gain, harmful graphs detected.

SAY THIS:
The public age archive contained 1,272 harmonised rows, of which 329 passed the strict reportability guard. Against the reported USGS and TracerLPM configurations, HydroSheaf achieved a median absolute log-ten age discrepancy of 0.0279, an R-squared of 0.937, and 87.5 percent agreement within a factor of two. This is close reference agreement, not formal equivalence and not independent age truth. The important integration test was whether graph information added value. The weak hydraulic proxy changed RMSE by only minus 0.00135 and worsened factor-two agreement, so it failed the improvement rule. A wrong-direction graph worsened RMSE by 0.1008, and a random graph worsened it by 0.6550. HydroSheaf therefore did not beat TracerLPM. It reproduced reported outputs closely and showed that unsupported topology can create negative transfer.

TRANSITION:
The next question was whether directed connectivity itself could be inferred from independent evidence.

For topology, MODPATH particle tracks supplied a model-conditioned reference network. The head-gradient inference achieved precision 0.49, recall 0.84 and F1 0.62, while negative controls were close to zero. The supported conclusion is conditional topology skill against MODPATH-derived reference transitions, not independently measured field connectivity.

Timing: 12:00-14:00

MEMORY ANCHOR: A low residual does not identify a unique mechanism.

SAY THIS:
The reaction benchmark used 240 live-PHREEQC scenarios and 21,600 inverse fits. The key result is that concentration fit and mechanism recovery are not the same. Conventional inverse PHREEQC produced, on average, 185.78 feasible models and 6.79 minimal models per scenario. Fifty-five percent of the lowest-residual fits still had phase F1 below 0.80. The guarded HydroSheaf result gave exact-phase F1 of 0.563, equivalence-class F1 of 0.609 and a false-discovery rate of 0.361. These values are not perfect, but they support a more defensible reporting target. Instead of selecting one apparently best mineral pathway, the method reports reaction families or equivalence classes and preserves the alternatives that the chemistry cannot distinguish.

TRANSITION:

Timing: 14:00-16:00

MEMORY ANCHOR: Fit stayed stable while identifiability collapsed.

SAY THIS:
Northern Ghana provided 320 records, of which 294 met the quantitative quality tier. The field question was not whether exact reactions could be validated, because independent reaction truth was unavailable. The question was which measurements controlled interpretive resolution. Under the predeclared evidence gate, removing strontium and silica moved approximately 52 percent of wells into the non-identifiable category. At the same time, the mean fit score remained around 68 to 71, bootstrap support remained high, and process labels changed in 35.6 percent of wells. A synthetic check supported the direction of this result, but the 52 percent value is an operational classification, not independently observed field truth. The scientific implication is important: a model can continue to fit the available observations while losing the information needed to distinguish processes.

TRANSITION:
The integration benchmark then tested directly whether additional evidence improved the inference or merely increased confidence.

Timing: 16:00-17:50

MEMORY ANCHOR: More data helped only when it supplied independent information.

SAY THIS:
In the independent integration generator, I tested each evidence stream by adding it to the others. Chemistry produced the clear topology-ranking gain: plus 0.447 PR-AUC, and this survived family-wise multiplicity correction. Hydraulics had a smaller point estimate of plus 0.0091. Its ranking contrast was not multiplicity-significant, with adjusted p equal to 0.070, although its Brier-score and log-loss improvements survived. Adding age gave a point estimate of minus 0.0060 and also did not survive multiplicity correction. Therefore the evidence streams were not equally informative. Chemistry carried strong independent ranking information in this generator. Hydraulics contributed mainly through calibration. Age added no positive topology-ranking value beyond hydraulics and chemistry. The broader lesson is that added data are not automatically added information.

TRANSITION:
The information flow also worked in the opposite direction: when topology was correct, it could condition age inference.

Timing: 17:50-19:10

MEMORY ANCHOR: Correct topology helped slightly; reversed topology harmed.

SAY THIS:
When correct topology was supplied to the age model, mean absolute error decreased by 0.0619 years with two tracers and by 0.1642 years with tritium alone. The uncertainty intervals also narrowed without a coverage penalty. These changes were statistically precise but practically small: approximately 2.24 and 3.46 percent of the respective baseline errors. The practical planning margins were added after review and were not prespecified. The result should therefore be described as a small conditional improvement, strongest under the weaker tracer panel. Reversing the topology increased error, reduced coverage and caused numerical instability in several tritium-only cases. Correct topology can reduce age non-uniqueness, but an unsupported graph can make age inference worse.

TRANSITION:

Timing: 19:10-21:30

MEMORY ANCHOR: Map semantics and conflict localisation, not universal superiority.

SAY THIS:
This is the central sheaf-versus-graph result. The affine sheaf improved PR-AUC by 0.0854 relative to an identity graph Laplacian. Native affine maps also beat permuted maps by 0.0909, showing that the learned map semantics mattered. The identity-limit cases matched exactly, so the sheaf properly reduced to the graph baseline when the restrictions were identity maps. However, the stronger edge-local weighted graph was a much more demanding comparator. Against it, the overall PR-AUC difference was only plus 0.0097 and the simultaneous confidence interval crossed zero. The complete superiority gate therefore failed. The supported contribution is narrower but real: edge-specific gain and offset relations, global compatibility testing, and improved localisation of planted cycle conflicts. HydroSheaf did not establish that a sheaf is universally more predictive than a strong weighted graph.

TRANSITION:
I also tested whether a more robust local-plus-global estimator could turn that conditional advantage into general superiority.

DELIVERY CUE: This is a high-stakes slide. State the positive evidence first, then volunteer the failed overall gate before anyone asks.

AVOID SAYING: Do not hide the edge-local comparator or describe the affine sheaf as the overall winner.

Timing: 21:30-22:45

MEMORY ANCHOR: Higher point estimate, corrected interval crosses zero, no general win.

SAY THIS:
Development selected a local-first, global-fallback estimator, and it was evaluated once on 128 fresh locked cases. The PR-AUC point estimate was 0.0200 higher than the edge-local graph, but the family-wise simultaneous interval ranged from minus 0.0055 to plus 0.0454. Brier score and log loss were also inconclusive, so the complete superiority gate failed. The leave-one-edge-out robust global method actually worsened calibration. Native maps still beat permuted maps, and conflict localisation remained useful, but this experiment did not convert the sheaf into a universal winner. I therefore report it as an estimator diagnostic and a direction for future refinement.

TRANSITION:
Taken together, the failures are not side notes; they define the scientific boundary of the thesis.

SAY THIS:
I began with the problem that separate analyses can produce plausible but incompatible groundwater stories. The thesis shows that HydroSheaf can bring those relations into one auditable framework. It can test whether the relations compose globally, quantify whether an added evidence stream contributes information, localise conflict, and reveal when apparently precise integration is confidently wrong. Its contribution is not universal superiority and it is not a fully validated Ghana aquifer model. The decisive next test is independent replication using a different generator family, or a matched field dataset containing environmental age tracers, repeated hydraulic observations, chemistry and independently measured connectivity. In summary, HydroSheaf provides a defensible way to integrate groundwater evidence while preserving the uncertainty and non-uniqueness that the data cannot resolve. Thank you.
